expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "Modal = Rung 2 (Warning). Adds friction to every delete and still doesn't stop the mistake"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "They develop click-through blindness and press 'Confirm' with the same reflex they press 'OK'"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "Soft-delete + trash = Rung 1 (Control). The mistake becomes reversible, so it needs no gate at all"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "Undo toast = Grace-period undo. Full recovery on the mistaken action, no friction on legitimate deletes"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: No dialog retained as option (rejects modal, does not propose alternative dialog with consequence info)

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
